headline: Google pulled premium Gemini models from free users; here's the cheapest fix
summary: As of October 9, free Gemini accounts no longer include 3.6 Flash and 3.1 Pro models, which are now reserved for paid subscribers. Free users are now limited to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite.
details: Until recently, free Gemini offered models like 3.6 Flash and 3.1 Pro, similar to what AI Plus subscribers received, with generous usage caps. This provided significant value without any cost.

However, this changed on October 9. Free personal Google accounts are now limited to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. This model is designed for speed and cost-efficiency, excelling at high-volume tasks such as translation and quick rewrites.

While 3.5 Flash-Lite is an improvement over its predecessor, it struggles with complex analytical problems or long chains of logic. Free accounts also face a 32,000-token context window, limiting Gemini to about 24,000 words before it starts losing context.

For those needing more capability, the AI Plus plan is recommended, now priced at $5/month (down from $8) and including 400GB of storage. This tier provides Gemini Flash, a substantial upgrade from Flash-Lite for coding and multi-step tasks.

AI Plus also offers a 128,000-token context window (approximately 190 pages) and integrates Gemini into Gmail for features like proofreading and AI Inbox. This plan is considered a strong value, especially for users invested in Google's ecosystem.

The AI Pro tier, at $20/month, targets developers and data analysts, granting access to Gemini 3.1 Pro and 3.8 Flash. It boasts a massive 1 million-token context window, capable of handling about 1,500 pages of text or 30,000 lines of code.

AI Pro users also receive four times the usage allowance of the free tier and 5TB of storage. This plan enhances limits in Antigravity, Google's agentic coding platform, and will soon include Deep Think, an extended reasoning mode previously exclusive to the $100/month AI Ultra tier.

headline: Pro-AI Super PAC Network Pours Millions Into Nevada Shell Companies
summary: A network of pro-AI super PACs, backed by major AI investors, has channeled over $140 million into political campaigns, with millions flowing to mysterious Nevada LLCs. Election watchdogs allege these are shell companies designed to mask the identities of cons
details: One of the biggest pro-AI super PAC networks has directed millions of dollars to a consulting agency, Lantern Production Consultants LLC, which appears to exist only as a post office box in a Nevada shopping center.

Lantern Production Consultants has received approximately $20 million since last year from Think Big, part of a network of pro-AI super PACs funded by the Leading the Future PAC. These funds were for services like polling, digital advertising, and strategy, according to federal campaign finance records.

This is just one of four mysterious Nevada-based LLCs that have received payments from the Leading the Future PAC network, which includes Think Big and American Mission. Other entities, like Summit Ridge Media Group LLC and Blue Horizon Compliance Consultants, list addresses at mail centers or retail stores.

Election watchdogs, including the Campaign Legal Center, argue these LLCs are shell companies intended to conceal the identities of strategists and consultants working with Leading the Future. They claim this practice hides the true recipients of the money.

In May, the Campaign Legal Center filed a complaint with the FEC, alleging that Think Big and American Mission violated federal law by failing to disclose the actual recipients of their payments. Leading the Future denies the allegations, calling them a "desperate ploy for attention."

Despite the complaint, the FEC has been unable to act due to a lack of a quorum, a situation that has persisted since May 2025. Meanwhile, the super PACs continue to funnel millions into these Nevada LLCs.

The Leading the Future network has raised over $140 million from Silicon Valley bankrollers like Marc Andreessen, Ben Horowitz, and OpenAI president Greg Brockman. It supports both Republican and Democratic candidates who align with an "AI innovation policy agenda."
